label: digit 1 mid-sequence in m-initial sequences after k/n/c context
predicate: (phase == 0) & (orig(0) == tok("m")) & (in_tok == tok("1")) & (t >= 4) & (t <= 6) & (isin(prev_tok, [tok("k"), tok("n"), tok("w")]) | isin(prev2_tok, [tok("k"), tok("n"), tok("c")]))
explanation: Very sparse, highly conjunctive feature (180 active steps on the dev split). It fires almost only in the original phase (97% of mass; never in the copy phase) at steps 4-6, in sequences whose first token is m (94% of mass). Its main trigger is the input digit 1 (70% of mass, 19x lift), most strongly when one of k, n or c came 1-2 steps before (e.g. m z c n k [1]). The largest activations are 1 preceded by k with c/n earlier in the sequence. Weak tail activations land on other tokens right after k in m-initial sequences, plus a few on <DEL>. It does not fire on 1 in sequences that start with another token, on 1 at steps 0-3 or 7+, or on most m...1 sequences without the k/n/c context: even the best predicate has dev precision of only ~0.33. Dev: P 0.33, R 0.39, F1 0.36, mass recall 0.55. The simpler predicate (first token m, input 1, t in 4-6) covers 0.62 of the mass at precision 0.08.
